title: Breakfast Quesadillas
subtitle: Crisp flour tortillas packed with eggs, bacon, and pepper jack.
description: Griddled quesadillas cut into wedges feed eight fast without plates full of crumbs. Scrambled eggs, crisp bacon, and pepper jack get pressed between flour tortillas until shatter-crisp outside and molten inside.

ingredients.name: sour cream
ingredients.notes: and salsa verde at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Quesadillas in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Bacon. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep the fillings
steps.instruction: Cook bacon until crisp, drain, and crumble. Soft-scramble eggs over medium-low heat—they should still look glossy. Drain pico well so quesadillas don't steam and split. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build on half the tortilla
steps.instruction: On one half of each tortilla, layer cheese, eggs, bacon, a spoon of pico, and more cheese. Fold over and press gently to compact without tearing. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Griddle until golden
steps.instruction: Heat a large griddle or skillet over medium with butter. Cook quesadillas 3–4 minutes per side with a spatula press until deeply golden and cheese melts through. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold and cut
steps.instruction: Transfer to a cutting board and rest 2 minutes so cheese sets. Cut each into 3 wedges with a sharp knife or pizza wheel. Hold warm on a sheet pan at 200°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Serve with dips
steps.instruction: Serve wedges with sour cream and salsa verde at the line. Keep crispy wedges uncovered; cover only if holding longer than 15 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Griddle two quesadillas at a time while a second cook builds the next pair—never stack uncooked folds.
Use a flat press or second spatula to maximize crust contact; pale quesadillas mean cold centers.
Cut on a dedicated board and slide wedges directly into a warm hotel pan for self-serve.
cleanupNotes: Wipe the griddle between batches with a damp towel and tongs to prevent burnt cheese buildup.
Drain pico through a fine mesh strainer over a bowl—wet salsa is the number-one cause of soggy quesadillas.
leftovers: Reheat wedges in a dry skillet over medium-low with a lid until cheese remelts—microwave makes them rubbery.
Chop leftover wedges into a breakfast nacho topping with extra cheese and pickled jalapeños.
